checklist.hint: Application-Pal never changes anything on LinkedIn – you transfer every item yourself. Whatever a new import can prove ticks itself afterwards.

checklist.setupGuide: Guide: set up your LinkedIn profile
checklist.setupHint: No LinkedIn profile yet? Set it up in this order. The texts (headline, About, positions) come from your draft further down.

account.title: Create the account
account.tip: Sign up with a private email address – not your school, university or employer address, which you will lose later. First and last name as on your CV. In the settings, add a second email address and turn on two-step verification.

quiet.title: Don't share profile updates yet
quiet.tip: While you build the profile: Settings → Visibility → turn off “Share profile updates with your network”, so your network doesn't see every intermediate step. Turn it back on later so that, for example, a new job gets announced.

url.title: Set your own profile URL
url.tip: On your profile, “Edit public profile & URL”: linkedin.com/in/firstname-lastname instead of a string of numbers. Then put the URL on your CV and in your email signature.

location.title: Set location and industry
location.tip: Use the city or region where you want to work as your location – recruiters filter by it. Pick the industry you want to start in.

education.title: Fill in education in detail
education.tip: Without much work experience, education is your strongest section: school or university, degree, field of study, dates – and in the description your focus, thesis and projects. Your draft provides the text.

practice.title: Add internships, jobs, volunteering and projects
practice.tip: Internships and side jobs go under Experience with the matching employment type (e.g. Internship, Part-time). Volunteering has its own “Volunteering” section, study and personal projects go under “Projects”. Add missing sections via “Add profile section”.

openTo.title: Set “Open to” deliberately
openTo.tip: Under “Open to” → “Finding a new job”, enter target roles, locations and workplace type. Then choose who sees it: recruiters only (discreet) or all members (green frame around your photo). Both are common – decide deliberately.

network.title: Make your first connections
network.tip: Connect with classmates and fellow students, teachers and lecturers, colleagues from internships and volunteering – each with a short personal note on how you know each other. A few relevant connections are worth more than many strangers.

follow.title: Follow companies, find alumni
follow.tip: Follow the companies you want to work for. On your school's or university's page, use “Alumni” to find graduates in your target field. One or two thoughtful comments a week make you visible before you post anything yourself.
